title: Sort Colors
summary: Given an array of n objects colored red, white, or blue, sort the objects in place so that objects of the same color are adjacent, with colors in the order red, white, and blue.
statement: Given an array of n objects colored red, white, or blue, sort the objects in place so that objects of the same color are adjacent, with colors in the order red, white, and blue. Use the integers 0, 1, and 2 to represent red, white, and blue, respectively. Solve this without using the library's sort function.
constraints: Reorder nums in place with 0s first, then 1s, then 2s. Do not use a library sort. Target one pass and constant extra space.
hints: Maintain finished regions for zeros and twos, with unknown values in between.
Use low, current, and high pointers: move 0 left, 2 right, and advance past 1.
A 0 swap advances low and current. A 2 swap decrements high but leaves current unchanged. A 1 advances current.
The value arriving from high is unclassified and must be examined before advancing.
editorial: Maintain zeros before low, ones between low and current, unknown values from current through high, and twos after high. Every operation reduces the unknown region. A swap with the high end brings in an unknown value, so do not advance current; a swap with low brings in an already classified value and can advance. The oracle sorts a separate copy; the learner-facing reference performs no sort call.

tests.explanation: Two occurrences of each color become [0,0,1,1,2,2] in the original list.
Move the one 0 to the front and the one 2 to the back, leaving [0,1,2].
